Eup-pur. * Full text (45 Ko) * Red and blue only * Red only

   

MIND. [1] [Eup. pur.]
Stupid, dull. θ Dropsy. θ Intermittent.
Confusion with falling to left side.
The mind encompassed by various delusions.
Talkative ; exclamations ; delusions of sight and hearing.
Sighing every few minutes, with gnawing at stomach.
Moaning ; suffering expressed by peculiar cries.
Hysterical mood, weeping, sighing, and a feeling like home sickness, though occupying her own home and surrounded by her own family, with fluttering of heart and a disagreeable fulness in throat.
Feels extremely depressed and sleepy.
Has a great fear of sickness.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Eup. pur.]
Head feels light and dizzy, as though flying round and round ; cannot get rid of the sensation as if falling towards the left side ; the whole body seems to participate.
Lightness of head < in morning, disappearing at 12 o'clock.
Sensation as if her head were moving in all directions.
Illusions of sight and hearing, with vertigo.
Confused, heavy ; cannot seem to prevent falling.
Dull, sleepy ; great effort required in order to move about.
   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Eup. pur.]
Dull, heavy pain in head ; most severe in forehead.
Much headache and constriction over frontal region, with chill.
Dizzy, with deep, dull, aching pain through temporal region on left side.
Vertex full, pressing, as though lifting up from adjoining parts.
Head feels as though she had a bad cold.
Hard thumping pain on left occipital bone.
Pain from left shoulder extends to occiput.
Sick headache ; dull hammering, beating, stitching, or boring pain in left side of head ; pressing from right to left ; beginning in morning and increasing during afternoon and evening ; < in cold air ; > while walking slowly in fresh air.
Violent headache : before the chill ; during morning ; with fever.
   

OUTER HEAD. [4] [Eup. pur.]
Fine pricking sensation on scalp, rather pleasurable than otherwise.
Soreness, tenderness, and itching of scalp.
Sweat, principally on head, particularly profuse about forehead.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Eup. pur.]
Staring ; looking with fixed eyes, wide open.
Cannot see as far as usual, with sleepy feeling.
Eyes weeping ; copious flow of tears.
Copious flow of tears, filling eyes, making constant wiping necessary.
Eyes red and swollen ; violent headache.
Conjunctiva yellow, with the chill.
   

HEARING AND EARS. [6] [Eup. pur.]
Ears feel as though they were full.
Squeaking sound in ears ; reports ; illusions of hearing.
Crackling, like burning of birch-bark ; very much < upon swallowing anything.
   

SMELL AND NOSE. [7] [Eup. pur.]
Fluent coryza ; great heat, sneezing.
Abundant discharge of a thin, watery fluid, making nose sore and irritable.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Eup. pur.]
Congestion to face, with burning heat, dry and hot to touch.
Face flushed, with fever.
Shining appearance of face, as when having used a large quantity of soap in washing.
   

LOWER FACE. [9] [Eup. pur.]
Lips blue. θ Intermittent.
   

TEETH AND GUMS. [10] [Eup. pur.]
Gums red and hot.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Eup. pur.]
Tongue furred, brown along centre ; bitter, pappy taste, with chill.
Pricking and stinging in end of tongue.
Fine pricking sensation on posterior part of tongue.
Numb feeling of tongue, as if caused by aconite.
   

INNER MOUTH. [12] [Eup. pur.]
Increased action of all the glands of the mouth ; abundance of saliva.
   

PALATE AND THROAT. [13] [Eup. pur.]
Fluttering in throat-pit ; extends upward from heart.
Disagreeable fulness in throat ; can hardly prevent crying.
Choking fulness of throat, must swallow often.
Swallowing : < crackling in ears ; causes pain.
Soreness, roughness and dryness in throat.
Sensation in throat as if having swallowed tobacco.
Burning, smarting, as if having been scalded by swallowing some hot substance.
Continued smarting and burning, most severe in posterior part of throat.
Pain in left side of throat, causing pain in swallowing ; before chill.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Eup. pur.]
No appetite ; much thirst.
Loss of appetite with fever ; desire to eat immediately after.
Thirst before the chill, none during.
Constant thirst with fever.
Thirst, in a case of dropsy.
Longing for lemonade, or cold acid drinks, with violent bone pains, blue lips and nails, extremities cold, and frontal headache.
Longing for hot drinks.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Eup. pur.]
Great quantity of wind in stomach ; eructations almost constant.
Great nausea and sickness of stomach, but no vomiting with the chill.
Nausea ; vomiting with fever.
Vomiting, with sick headache.
